subject: history
angle: The sugar industry sponsored research in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt on the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the primary cause of coronary heart disease.
title: The funded narrative of sugar

hooks.text: Who funded your heart health advice?
You were told fat was the problem, but the industry funded that shift.
You are following a narrative paid for by the sugar industry.
A soda sits on a table while the research is hidden.
57.30 times more likely to find no harm.

reveal.headline: The sugar industry funded research to cast doubt on sucrose hazards.
reveal.body: During the 1960s and 1970s, industry-sponsored programs successfully promoted fat as the primary cause of coronary heart disease while downplaying the risks of sugar.

explain.headline: Industry-related studies were more likely to find no harm.
explain.body: Studies linked to the industry were overwhelmingly more likely to reach weak or null conclusions regarding the effects of sugar-sweetened beverages compared to independent research.

matters.headline: The narrative on heart health was shaped by funding.
matters.body: That may be why the focus on fat became the standard dietary advice while the risks of sucrose remained less explored by the public.

example.headline: A soda on a kitchen table.
example.body: You reach for a sugar-sweetened beverage in the afternoon. You assume the fat content is the main concern for your heart health.

claims.text: The Sugar Research Foundation (SRF) funded a review in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1965 that discounted evidence linking sucrose consumption to blood lipid levels and coronary heart disease.
claims.quote: In 1965, the Sugar Research Foundation (SRF) secretly funded a review in the New England Journal of Medicine that discounted evidence linking sucrose consumption to blood lipid levels and hence coronary heart disease (CHD).

claims.text: The sugar industry sponsored a research program in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt about the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the dietary culprit in CHD.
claims.quote: our findings suggest the industry sponsored a research program in the 1960s and 1970s that successfully cast doubt about the hazards of sucrose while promoting fat as the dietary culprit in CHD.

claims.text: Industry-related studies were overwhelmingly more likely to reach 'weak/null' conclusions compared with independent studies regarding the adverse effects of SSB consumption on health (OR=57·30, 95 % CI 7·12, 461·56).

verdict: The evidence shows that the sugar industry actively funded and influenced research to downplay the risks of sucrose and shift the blame for heart disease toward fat.
caveat: The research on the health effects of sugar-sweetened beverages shows a significant decrease in industry-related studies over time.
caption: The sugar industry influenced how you view heart disease. Research shows they funded programs in the 1960s and 1970s to promote fat as the culprit while discounting the hazards of sucrose. While the proportion of industry-related studies has decreased significantly over time, the historical influence remains. What does this mean for the choices you make today?
